questions.question:

questions.solution:

• **'Are' **is used for plural subjects, whereas '**am**' is used for singular subjects.
 
• The verb must agree with its subject in number and person. When two subjects are joined by ‘**AND**’, the verb is plural.
 
• In the given sentence, **Adam and I (2 people) are plural subjects**, so the plural verb (**are**) should be used.
 
• We use the pronoun "**I**" when the person speaking is doing the action, either alone or with someone else.
 
• We use the pronoun "**me**" when the person speaking is receiving the action of the verb in some way, either directly or indirectly.
 
• **'Planning' **is an action, so the correct form is **"Adam and I are planning a grand party at our office."**
 
• ​**Therefore, the given sentence is both grammatically and conceptually correct.**

Hence, the correct answer is **option 4**.

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.**

Over the years, the threat of cyberattacks on satellites has gotten more direr.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **has gotten more direr**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Replace "**direr**" with "**dire**" to correct the sentence.
 
• **Dire **means extremely serious or urgent.
 
 
• **Example -** *Misuse of drugs can have dire consequences.*
 
 
 
• We use "**more**" to indicate that there is a greater amount of something than before or than average, or than something else.
 
• In the given sentence there is a comparison between past years and the current scenario.
 
• **More **is a comparative form. Also, "Direr" is the comparative degree of "dire"
 
• The use of two comparatives together is incorrect.
 
• Therefore, only one comparative form should be used.
 
• So, "dire" will be used in place of "direr".

Hence, the correct answer is **option 2** which contains an error.

**Corrected sentence:** *Over the years, the threat of cyberattacks on satellites has gotten more dire.*

questions.question:

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Gently **means with a mild, kind, or tender manner. It is an adverb.
 
• An **adverb **is used to provide more information about the verb or the action in the sentence.
 
• In the given sentence the question is "How to put the baby on the bed?" and the obvious answer will be "very gently"
 
• We use '**very**' before adverbs and adjectives to add emphasis. It means to a great degree.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

__
 
• **Gentle **is an adjective, which means having or showing a mild, kind, or tender temperament or character.
 
• We use **adjectives **to describe nouns. Most adjectives can be used in front of a noun.
 
• We never use "very gentle" in a sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The word '**much**' refers to a large amount or plenty of something.
 
• The word '**more**' is the comparative degree of much/many. It means a greater amount of something. It can be used as an Adjective, an Adverb, a Noun, a Determiner, or a Pronoun.
 
• In the given sentence, "**very**" is already mentioned. So, we cannot use "**much**" and "**more**" with it.

Therefore, the most appropriate option to fill in the blank is "**gently**."

Hence, the correct answer is** option 2**.

**Complete sentence:** *You need to put the baby very **gently __**on the bed.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.**

As a young girl, Mary lived in France, where __she have married__ the king of France, Francis II.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **she married** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Remove the irregular verb "**have**" to correct the sentence.
 
• **Have **is used with the pronouns I, you, we, and they.
 
• **Has **is used with he, she, and it.
 
• We use "**have/has + V3**" in the **present perfect tense** to indicate an action as completed or a state as having ended before a specified or implied time in the past.
 
• **Past simple** expresses actions that occurred in the past, while **past perfect** talks about something that occurred before another past event or action.
 
• **The implied meaning of the given sentence is:** Mary spent her formative years in France, where she later wed Francis II, the country's monarch.
 
• From here, we can say that the given sentence is talking about an event that occurred in the past a long time ago. So, the sentence should be written in the "**simple past tense**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] **Mistake Points__**

 
• We should always use the "**Simple Present"** form of the verb with “**did**”.
 
• Using "**did + V3**" is grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**, which will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

**Corrected sentence:** *As a young girl, Mary lived in France, where she married the king of France, Francis II.*
